text:
Alice: ok team — sketching a pragmatic rollout for the regional canary + opt-in shadowing ask from AcmeCorp. want agreement on safety gates, customer opt-in UX, and fallback chain. TL;DR: phased regional canary (5% -> 20% -> 50%), parallel shadow traffic for opt-ins, automatic fallback to cheaper model variant + cross-region spillover, and a kill-switch if telemetry gates trip.

Ben: sounds good. question: do we do A/B for quality (two prompts/models) or standard canary with model-variant fallback?

Alice: prefer canary with shadow A/Bting for quality where customers opt-in. keep primary path simple for latency-sensitive traffic.

Carmen: telemetry gates we should enforce: p95 latency > baseline + 200ms, error rate (5xx) increase > 0.5pp, and regression on prompt evals (we run a small eval set every 15m). if any gate trips, immediate throttle to 0 for the canary slice + trigger human paging.

Diego: for the prompt evals — recommend we run both: (1) automated heuristic checks (toxicity / hallucination quick scorers) and (2) sampled human review for top 50 failure candidates per hour (only for opt-ins).

Elaine: customer ops: AcmeCorp asked to opt-in selected teams during their business hours only and to have a per-tenant toggle. they also want a rollback email to be delivered to their SRE on failure.

Ben: ops question — can we do per-tenant opt-in without creating N feature flags? we should reuse the tenant flagging system and a single rollout-policy that references tenant cohorts.

Alice: agreed. single flag + cohort list. per-tenant exemption list for enterprise customers who want to skip canaries.

Carmen: fallback chain proposal (priority order):
1) serve traced requests to model-variant quantized-2 (fast) with same API signatures
2) route to next-region warm pool (same model family)
3) degrade to cached responses for prefix-y hits (300ms SLA)
4) return polite degrade message: "We're experiencing higher load right now — try again in a few seconds"
If any step executed, log telemetry event with reason_code and magnitude.

Ben: add-on: include token-cost delta check. if cost-per-token spikes > 30% vs baseline, we treat as a soft gate (warn + reduce traffic fraction).

Diego: here's a sample flag config I sketched (pseudo):
```
feature: regional_canary_acmecorp
enabled: true
default_fraction: 0.0
stages:
  - name: stage-1
    fraction: 0.05
    regions: [us-west-2]
    telemetry_gates: [p95_latency, error_rate, eval_regressions, cost_delta]
  - name: stage-2
    fraction: 0.20
    regions: [us-west-2, us-east-1]
  - name: stage-3
    fraction: 0.50
    regions: [global]
per_tenant_overrides: { 'acmecorp-team-a': 1.0 }
kill_switch: /ops/rollout-kill
```

Alice: nice. we also need a baked-in hold window after each stage: 60m minimum + 2 successful telemetry cycles. no automatic advance until telemetry is green.

Carmen: define "successful telemetry cycle": p95 within threshold, error rate stable, and no eval regression in last 30m sample. we should also check tail latency histogram shifts (bucketed check).

Elaine: for the customer-facing opt-in UX: a toggle in Console under their account, with the ability to schedule windows (start/end times), plus email notifications on stage changes and rollbacks. also provide a small dashboard widget with the four telemetry KPIs.

Ben: deployment ops — during stage advancement, we do rolling restarts limited to 5% of dedicated pools to avoid correlated cache misses. and pre-warm KV caches for the new variant during the shadow window.

Diego: telemetry instrumentation notes: tag every request with rollout_id and cohort_id, sample 1% of full tokens to store for offline quality evals, keep sampled prompts for 7 days. also emit `rollout.transition` events for each stage change.

Alice: escalation plan: any stage failure auto-opens a P1 pager to the oncall SRE and the product owner. manual rollback must be possible in Console (single click) and via API (`POST /rollouts/{id}/kill`).

rollout-bot: deploy-check: preflight OK. US-WEST-2 pool has capacity for stage-1 (quota=180r/s). will schedule canary window at 2025-09-15T14:00Z unless cancelled.

Carmen: small note — ensure logs include the fallback_reason string for every fallback request; we need those for SLO reporting.

Ben: telemetry gates need thresholds per-region (baseline differs). also add synthetic traffic for baseline population during quiet hours.

Alice: decisions summary (so we have a ship-able spec):
- mechanism: phased regional canary with optional per-tenant opt-in shadowing
- stages: 5% -> 20% -> 50% with 60m hold + 2 green cycles
- telemetry gates: p95 latency, error rate, eval regressions, cost_delta, tail histogram check
- fallback chain: model-variant -> cross-region -> cached responses -> polite degrade
- kill-switch: Console + API + auto-pager on gate failure
- customer UX: per-tenant schedule + dashboard + email notifications
- instrumentation: rollout_id/cohort_id tags, sampled prompts, rollout.transition events

Elaine: can we get a short runbook for the customer-facing email content? i can draft if you want.

Alice: yes please. also Ben/Diego/Carmen — can you confirm engineering acceptance criteria by tomorrow EOD? I want this in the PM spec doc before stakeholder review on Friday.

Ben: will do.

Carmen: ✅ confirming SRE acceptance criteria in the doc now.

Diego: I'll add the eval harness and sampling knobs.

Elaine: I'll draft the email + dashboard mockups and drop in the spec.

rollout-bot: reminder: preflight window will send an auto-notice to `#product` 15m before scheduled canary start.

Alice: thanks everyone — great alignment. we should include a small A/B shadow experiment (opt-in only) to validate quality uplift claims, but keep the primary canary path single-variant for simplicity. leaving action items in the spec doc.
